page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highcpu-2 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 2 vCPUs and 4.0 GB of RAM. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using the x86_64 architecture, this instance allocates 1 physical core with 2 threads per core on a dedicated basis. The CPU configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core tests placing in the top 25 percent at 2921.98. However, multi-core and memory-bound operations show significant limitations. The stress-ng multi-core performance of 2926.09 and Geekbench multi-core score of 2013.0 both rank in the bottom 25 percent and bottom 10 percent respectively, reflecting the constraints of a single physical core. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with read-only small block cached bandwidth at 136.6 GB/sec and large block uncached write bandwidth at 23.42 GB/sec.

This instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring dedicated CPU cycles but minimal memory footprints. Single-threaded tasks such as gzip compression and bzip3 decompression perform at average levels, as does text processing and small-model LLM text generation. Conversely, database operations, software compilation, and memory-intensive tasks perform poorly due to the low 2.0 GB of RAM per core and low memory bandwidth. It is best suited for lightweight single-threaded processing, basic web serving, or small-scale background tasks that benefit from dedicated CPU allocation without high memory demands.
